description: LAG/LEAD with a non-null default (third argument) cannot return NULL when the tracked column is NOT NULL, because the default is returned instead of NULL at partition boundaries

columns.name: prev_amount
columns.note: LAG(amount, 1, 0) returns the literal default 0 instead of NULL at the partition boundary

columns.name: next_amount
columns.note: LEAD(amount, 1, 0) returns the literal default 0 instead of NULL at the partition boundary

name: lag_lead_default_narrows_non_null
query_sql:
-- @name LagLeadWithDefault
-- @returns :many
SELECT id, amount, LAG(amount, 1, 0) OVER (ORDER BY sale_date) AS prev_amount, LEAD(amount, 1, 0) OVER (ORDER BY sale_date) AS next_amount FROM sales
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE sales (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, employee_id INTEGER NOT NULL, department TEXT NOT NULL, amount INTEGER NOT NULL, discount INTEGER, sale_date DATE NOT NULL)

sqlc_comparison.scythe_improvement: scythe recognizes that a non-null third argument (default) to LAG/LEAD is returned at partition boundaries instead of NULL, so the result is non-nullable when the tracked expression is also non-null
sqlc_comparison.sqlc_behavior: sqlc does not model the LAG/LEAD default argument and marks the result nullable unconditionally, even when a non-null default guarantees a value
